label: prf:derived-mass-formula-light-isotopes
title: Proof of derived mass formula light isotopes
html:
Proof. The constituent baseline Z \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} + N \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z m_e uses CODATA inputs.

The Wedderburn 3-term correction is the paper's Wedderburn mass formula with \alpha = m_e \cdot 8G from binding scale. The functionals \Phi_1, \Phi_2, \Phi_3 are evaluated using only inter-nucleon generators of the atomic braid: this convention isolates inter-nucleon interactions, and ensures free nucleons (A = 1) contribute exactly zero to \Phi (preserving the constituent baseline inputs and the proton-neutron mass splitting exactly).

\Delta_W is the paper's Wigner T=0 np pairing for the self-conjugate partition (2,2) \vdash 4. \Delta_{T=1} is the natural extension to T=1 same-flavor pairs using the same partition and the same \min/A structure, replacing \min(Z,N) (number of T=0 pn pairs) by n_{pp} + n_{nn} (number of T=1 same-flavor pairs).

canonical evaluation at q_0 = 1.1099785955541805\ldots (50 dps; the CODATA-2018 muon pin recorded in the witness, which now sits in computations/_deprecated/) uses the formal derivation (witness derived-only-formula.witness.json). \square

Witness: derived-only-formula.witness.json.

Scope. The formula is derived from Hecke partition theory and the paper's atomic-mass framework; no continuous parameters are fitted, and no choices were made by selecting from a menu of variants. The atomic mass agreement to sub-percent across A = 1 to 7 — including the unfitted extension to ^6Li and ^7Li — is predictive, not calibrated.

The systematic binding under-prediction is the formula's principal limitation. Closed-form patches that improve specific isotopes (D, T, ^3He, ^4He) to within 7% can be constructed from H_q((2,1)) and [3]_q^2 candidates (see witnesses the formal derivation, the formal derivation, the formal derivation), but each such patch involves a discrete choice between several algebraically-natural variants — hence is technically fitted (model selection).

Structural extension to A \geq 5. The shell-correction conjecture (Term 7 shell correction) identifies the binding gap at A \geq 5 with the GB-filtration level \ell = 5 (height-6 partitions) of the brane-tower spectral sequence. Adding the conjectural Term 7 to the formula above is expected to bridge the binding gap structurally; the specific shadow-price form is open research.
